products.name: Falcon
products.captures: Stills of vehicles, plate text and state, vehicle description
products.not: No live video, no faces, no audio
products.note: Standard, Wide-Range (SR) and Long-Range (LR) variants; LR is sold for highways at $5,000 per year

products.name: Falcon Flex
products.captures: Same as Falcon, 14 Ah internal battery, ~30,000 reads per charge, 16 GB local buffer
products.not: No solar by default; band-clamp kit

products.name: Sparrow
products.captures: Same pipeline, marketed to HOAs and apartment entrances
products.not: Private customers cannot see law-enforcement data; they can share their own

products.name: Condor
products.captures: Live and recorded video, dual lens (90° context + 32x zoom), AI person detection and following
products.not: Not a plate reader by itself; Flock's statement that its cameras focus on vehicles rather than people refers to the plate readers

products.name: Raven
products.captures: Rolling ~3 s audio windows analysed on device for gunshots; only event clips are uploaded
products.not: Flock states it cannot interpret speech; a piloted human-distress detection feature was withdrawn in 2026

products.name: Wing
products.type: Software and gateway for existing cameras
products.captures: Vehicle Fingerprint attributes from any RTSP camera a customer already owns
products.not: No new camera; the configuration in which PoE, fiber and SFP modules are used

products.name: Alpha (drone as first responder)
products.captures: Live video and in-flight plate reads from roughly 2,000 ft
products.not: Different product; folded into the same FlockOS platform

products.name: Nova
products.captures: Data fusion from public records, open-source intelligence and commercial datasets, linking a plate to a registered person
products.not: No hardware; 404 Media reported in May 2025 that Flock stated it would not use breached-data sources
